This game really had my hopes up.... It really did. There was one small problem... THIS GAME WAS LITERALLY THE DEATH OF DAYZ. The game plays just as clunky as arma.. and some like that but clunky"ness" combined with the trash servers divided by the actual good things that Dayz (Mod) had goin for it such as base building or other custom mods or just the ability to multiply the amount of loot server TO SERVER... You just end up with a really really flawed game... It just feels like so bland... the first time i played, years ago... i found an M4 and a bunch of other gear.... I never saw that kind of loot again. the most i would find was a break action shotgun or some bullshit to be sniped by a guy with mil gear and a gillie suit.... again it just feels bland... wheres the team work... wheres the radios to call for help and team up... where is Epoch... WHERE IS DAYZ. this game was just not ever needed just a cop out to take something that you already pay for (ArmaOA) and make you feel like you need to pay again to get the true DayZ experience. Please dont buy this game.... Please.... my pain was ended after i was falsely banned under another persons in game username.

The game has been almost two years in development and it is still has alpha version. Melee-fights are still clumsy, you can't predict where your AI opponent will strike due to laggy movement animations. No vehicle diversity. Character animations are nothig close to an AAA-game made by a large group of devs which made huge money on pre-oders. Regular patches only include new hats and nothing more significant. That is a fact. At the meantime dayz-mod was much better optimized/coded and had a great loot/vehicle diversity without useless rubbish like books. You can't see any game-mechanics polishing because there is no polishing at all. Price is increasing, game quality is not. There is no excuse for devs for not doing their job properly through the years. Save your monies lads.

Yes the game is still in alpha stage after 2 years. And yes there are some gltches and bugs here and there. And of course, 35$ is too much for a game which is still in alpha stage after 2 years.

But no other survival MMO game comes close to this one.

Get this game if:
--> You dont mind dying again and agaiin but prefer to avoid and counter the effects which lead to death.
--> If you have patience to withstand small but not game breaking bugs.
--> If you love survival games and always wanted to play in massive world in which other players can join too (and not just AI)
--> If you have decent system which can at least run this game in playable state (even if you have to lower down settings)
--> If you have a couple of friends who can hang out with you (solo scavenging is good too but gets lonely sometimes unless you wanna play bandit style)

But yea, unless you really want to get this game, wait for discounted price.

12 000 HOUR REVIEW: This game is better than all other games ever. I have played through every stage of it's development. every "game breaking" bug. none ever stopped me from having fun. It taught me how to be socially manipulative in new and interesting ways. It's basically Arma so the gun play is realistic AF compared to the "plasticy" feeling of other pvp contemporaries. But challenging survival mechanics and languid social interactions place it uniquely in a genre of it's own. And the Chernarus map is one of the largest sandbox maps since Skrym. I paid like $19 for it 6 years ago and when i hit 10 000 hours i bought another copy because the devs deserved it. DayZ dev hating has become somewhat of a sport in the community, but none of the big dev companies are coming even close to what these guys have achieved... and if they are, like perhaps Red Dead or Star Citizen, the pricetag is waaaaay more than a humble copy of DayZ. And the new Livonia DLC is totally worth buying for the thousands of players who didnt get it in some obscure Arma pack way back when who give a fk jesus just enjoy yourselves dammit.

I have played DayZ in various iterations (console, arma mod) for a long time, and I've come to the conclusion that it is possibly the most underrated game in existence. Its not because of great mechanics, storyline or construction, but rather the dynamic ability to choose your own adventure. The beauty of the game comes not from killing everyone you see, but from finding someone, trusting them and becoming reliant on each other. There is nothing else quite like it. In 2021 I was diagnosed with a Stage 3 malignant carcinoma, and during the quite brutal chemo and radiation treatment, this game became a bit of a daily ritual for me. In some of my darkest moments, facing my own mortality, someone who I found in game, trusted and ran with for many months became a voice of strength when I needed it most. There is no other game like it.

Do yourself a favour, play the game with a sense of adventure and you might find that the greatest experience you can have online is to place trust in a random stranger and discover the best of humanity for it.

There's no other game that can really emulate that feeling of hopelessness surrounded by utter nothingness not knowing whether or not you'll be killed minutes or hours. It keeps you on your toes and from what it has been, the game is leagues better than it was.
